My answer is in `final.py`. It scored **72.3 on the search split** (1.32 s CPU for the reference against 0.018 s for mine) and used **2 of the 24 scorer calls**. Both runs were valid, so every pair matched the reference. The final score will come from instances I haven't seen.

**How it works:** it uses the standard "prefix filtering" method for finding similar sets, so it only does the exact check on likely pairs instead of comparing every pair.
- Words are ranked from rarest to most common across the whole catalogue, and each record's words are put in that order.
- Records are processed from fewest words to most. A record is only compared with earlier ones that share a word in its first few rarest words. How many words count depends on its size and the 80% threshold.
- A record is also skipped when its size alone rules out 80% similarity.
- Every remaining candidate gets the exact check from the docstring, `5·|A∩B| ≥ 4·|A∪B|`, so the result is exact. Records with no words are never indexed.

**Testing:** before scoring, I checked it against the reference on 3,000 small random inputs with edge cases (empty records, mixed whitespace, repeated words). I also checked one generated input of about 3,500 records, where it ran about 60 times faster. Everything matched.

My second scored call was a micro-optimised version that came out the same (72.0). At 18 ms, I think fixed overhead is now most of the time, so further tuning wouldn't gain much. I kept the simpler first version and deleted the second one and my test script.

I wrote that test script in `/tmp` for a moment before moving it into the task folder. I didn't read any file outside the folder.

The Atlassian Rovo and HyperFrames by HeyGen connectors need authorising in your claude.ai connector settings before they can be used. This task didn't need them.
